title: Fui a México
blurbEn: The trip finally happens. Here come the irregular preterites — and the strangest one: 'fui' is both 'I went' and 'I was'.
body:
El año pasado fui a México por fin.

Fue un viaje largo. Estuve muchas horas en el avión y llegué al aeropuerto muy cansada.

Pablo me esperó allí con su familia. Tuve mucha suerte: ellos me invitaron a su casa y no pagué nada de hotel.

Estuvimos una semana en Ciudad de México y después fuimos a la playa.

La comida fue increíble y la gente fue muy amable conmigo. Tuve que aprender muchas palabras nuevas, pero mereció la pena.
translationEn:
Last year I finally went to Mexico.

It was a long trip. I spent many hours on the plane and arrived at the airport very tired.

Pablo waited for me there with his family. I was very lucky: they invited me to their house and I did not pay anything for a hotel.

We spent a week in Mexico City and afterwards we went to the beach.

The food was incredible and the people were very kind to me. I had to learn many new words, but it was worth it.

fui.note: 'ir' and 'ser' share exactly the same preterite. 'Fui a México' is I went; 'Fui feliz' is I was happy. Context decides, always.

fue.note: Same form as 'he/she went'. Here it is 'ser' — 'fue un viaje largo'.

Estuve.note: From 'estar'. Irregular stem 'estuv-' plus its own set of endings, with no accents.

Tuve.note: From 'tener'. Stem 'tuv-' — the same pattern as 'estuve'.

phrases.note: Spanish *has* luck rather than *is* lucky, just as it has years rather than is them.
